pages.title: FreeCAD document structure
pages.subtitle: At least two Bodies are required
items: A Body holding the groove — shaft or bore depending on the case.
A Body for the mating part — bore or shaft, i.e. the complementary case.
Each Body is fully modelled at its nominal size, with no groove.
The document is saved and recomputed without errors (Model → Refresh).
pages.tip: The macro creates the groove itself. Do not sketch it manually beforehand.

pages.title: Mandatory named parameters
pages.subtitle: One radius or diameter parameter in each Body
items: In each relevant Body, a named parameter must exist to define the radius or diameter of the sealing surface.
This parameter must be linked to the Body geometry — the macro uses it to compute squeeze and size the groove.
The macro will ask you to select this parameter from a drop-down list — short, descriptive names are recommended (e.g. D_shaft, R_bore).
pages.tip: If the parameter represents a radius, prefix it with R_ or r_ — the macro adjusts its calculation accordingly.

pages.title: Local Coordinate System (LCS)
pages.subtitle: Axial positioning reference for the groove
items: Insert an LCS (Local Coordinate System) in the groove-bearing Body, at the exact location of the desired groove mid-plane.
The Z axis of the LCS must be aligned with the part's revolution axis — i.e. the groove's axis of symmetry.
The LCS can be constrained to a face, a reference plane or positioned by dimension — as long as it follows the axial parameter of the part.
Give the LCS a meaningful name — the macro lists all LCS objects available in the selected Body.

pages.title: Technical service data
pages.subtitle: Have these ready before opening the dialog

pages.title: Final checklist
pages.subtitle: Before clicking "Launch macro"
items: FreeCAD set to Standard unit system (mm, kg, s, °) — menu Edit → Preferences → General → Units.
Both Bodies recomputed with no yellow warning triangle or error icon in the model tree.
The LCS is positioned at the exact groove mid-plane, Z axis aligned with the revolution axis.
Service data (pressure, fluid, assembly type) are known.
pages.tip: All set? Close this guide and click Launch macro in the main dialog.
